# v0.3.4 Conversion Quality and macOS Release Plan

**Goal:** Close the remaining conversion-quality gaps, validate the supplied complex PDF by cell position, and publish unsigned macOS arm64/x64 builds together with the corrected Windows and Win7 packages.

**Rule:** Every task starts with a failing test. A generated file is not proof of conversion quality; assertions must inspect structure, content, metadata, warnings, and platform boundaries.

## Task 1: Structured conversion warnings

- Add a small conversion-result helper that normalizes `warnings` and safe `details`.
- Preserve existing `error`, `errorCode`, and bilingual messages.
- Return warnings for animation flattening, lossy spreadsheet export, and experimental formats.
- Render bilingual warnings with `textContent`; never use `innerHTML`.
- Test API serialization, batch rendering, standard packaging, and Win7 staging.

## Task 2: Text conversion fidelity

- Replace the hand-written Markdown-to-HTML subset with a pinned parser supporting headings, emphasis, strong text, links, ordered/unordered lists, and fenced code.
- Extend the shared Turndown helper: simple HTML/DOCX tables become Markdown tables; rowspan/colspan tables remain safe HTML.
- Flatten nested JSON deterministically for CSV using dot notation; arrays remain JSON strings and never become `[object Object]`.
- Add unit and server integration tests before implementation.

## Task 3: Image and animation contracts

- Inspect frame/page metadata before conversion.
- Static outputs use the first composited frame and return an animation-flattened warning.
- JPEG always composites alpha onto an explicit white default and reports that choice.
- PNG/WebP/TIFF transparency tests inspect pixels.
- Advertise animated WebP/TIFF only if frame count and delay survive a real round trip; otherwise remove those target pairs from capabilities and docs.

## Task 4: Office output validation

- Presentation-to-HTML must contain a non-empty body and recognizable slide text; empty exports fail with a stable code.
- XLSX-to-CSV records the exported sheet and warns about omitted sheets and formulas after inspecting the workbook.
- Add real LibreOffice tests using an empty application-owned profile and assert no new soffice process/profile survives.

## Task 5: NCM metadata and platform boundary

- Preserve normalized title, artist, album, and cover bytes from NCM decryption.
- Map metadata into FFmpeg output and attach cover art for compatible containers.
- Assert metadata with a real official-client NCM fixture.
- Standard NCM remains cross-platform; AV3A decode is Windows-only in capabilities, UI, README, and tests.

## Task 6: Supplied complex PDF acceptance

- Copy the user-supplied scan into ignored test evidence; never commit private content without explicit permission.
- Build an expected-cell manifest using page/table/row/column coordinates, sheet names, merge ranges, warnings, and Raw fallbacks.
- Require electronic PDF cell accuracy >=95%, scanned PDF >=85%, and exact table count/sheet/explicit merge regions.
- If the sample fails, fix extraction heuristics with synthetic RED fixtures that isolate each geometry defect before rerunning the private sample.

## Task 7: Claims and experimental formats

- Mark HEIC, WPS/WPT/WPD, ET/ETT, DPS/DPT, and KGG as unverified/experimental until real fixtures pass.
- Keep KGG out of core marketing claims.
- Update bilingual UI, capabilities, README, architecture, release, and handoff without claiming physical-device acceptance.

## Task 8: macOS engine and package layout

- Make engine paths platform/architecture aware and keep environment overrides.
- Pin separate arm64/x64 engine archives and SHA-256 values; fail closed on wrong Mach-O architecture.
- Package unsigned, unnotarized DMGs for macOS 11+: `FlyingMouse Format-Setup-0.3.4-mac-arm64.dmg` and `...-mac-x64.dmg`.
- Exclude the Windows AVS3 decoder from macOS resources and tests.
- Run native GitHub-hosted arm64/x64 tests, probes, representative conversions, bundle inspection, and launch smoke.

## Task 9: Windows/Win7/macOS release gates

- Restore locked engines; run engine-free CI, full conversions, real NCM/AV3A, audits, syntax, and diff checks.
- Build standard NSIS/APPX, then Node 22 Win7 staging/installer; verify PE, ASAR, resources, icon, Office profile, and smoke.
- Let both native macOS jobs produce validated DMGs.
- Only then set version 0.3.4, merge/push main, create tag/release, upload four GitHub assets, and read back names/sizes/SHA-256/download URLs.
- Do not update the Microsoft Store in this GitHub-first phase. Mark Win7 and macOS physical-device acceptance as pending when no real device was used.
